setting: A co-op AI teammate (a bot) in a tactical shooter like Rainbow Six Siege or Counter-Strike. The human player places markers (pings) on the map and gives voice orders in English. The voice goes through speech-to-text; the bot receives the transcript (and, separately, the latest marker position). The bot must map each transcript to exactly one intent below; its planner then works out how to carry it out (which window, which route, where the marker is). Words like 'here', 'there', 'that', 'this' usually refer to the latest marker or to where the player is looking; the planner resolves them.

intents.FOLLOW_ME: the bot follows the player and stays with them. 'Look at me' is LOOK_AT_ME: the bot turns, it does not come
intents.MOVE_TO: the bot moves to a place: the marker, or a named or pointed-at location (a door, stairs, a floor, the roof)
intents.HOLD_POSITION: the bot stays where it is and stops moving
intents.HOLD_ANGLE: the bot watches a specific angle / door / window / corridor / stairs, ready to shoot, and keeps watching it. Only turning to look at something is LOOK_AT
intents.HOLD_OTHER_ANGLE: the bot watches the OTHER angle than the one currently covered (by the player or by the bot), e.g. the player takes one door and tells the bot to take the other
intents.FLANK: the bot takes an alternative route around to hit the enemy from the side or behind, often via the marker
intents.VAULT_WINDOW: the bot goes in or out through a window (vault, climb, jump through)
intents.RAPPEL: the bot uses a rappel rope on the outside of the building (rope up, drop down, hang at a window). Just going to a named place, the roof included, is MOVE_TO
intents.BREACH: the bot opens a wall, floor hatch, ceiling or barricaded door with a breaching charge or tool (loud)
intents.DRONE: the bot sends a drone or scouts to gather intel before anyone goes in
intents.FLASH: the bot throws a flashbang / stun grenade
intents.SMOKE: the bot throws a smoke grenade
intents.FRAG: the bot throws a lethal grenade (frag, molotov, incendiary)
intents.COVER_ME: the bot covers the PLAYER (watches over them, ready to shoot) while the player moves or does something
intents.ENTRY: the bot pushes into the room / site and clears it. A bare 'attack' that names no way is ATTACK
intents.FALL_BACK: the bot retreats / breaks off from the fight
intents.PLANT: the bot plants the bomb / defuser
intents.DEFUSE: the bot defuses the bomb / disables the defuser
intents.REVIVE_ME: the bot comes to revive the downed player
intents.WAIT: the bot pauses: stop what you are doing, hold up, do not act yet, cancel the last order. Only stopping the shooting is HOLD_FIRE
intents.GO_NOW: the bot executes the prepared or announced action right now; the player's go signal
intents.TAKE_COVER: the bot gets ITSELF into cover or out of sight to protect itself (hide, get behind something solid, get down); its planner picks the spot: the nearest cover, or the marker if the player points at one. Protecting the player is COVER_ME, not this
intents.OPEN: the bot opens a door, window, hatch, gate or shutter the normal way (by hand, quietly) and does NOT go through it; its planner picks which one. Going through a window is VAULT_WINDOW, pushing into the room is ENTRY, forcing it open with a charge or tool is BREACH
intents.ATTACK: the bot attacks the enemy, and HOW is left to its planner (push in, breach, or shoot from where it is): the player only says to attack / engage / take them out and names no way. If the player names the way, it is that intent instead: pushing into a room is ENTRY, a charge is BREACH, a grenade is FRAG, opening fire is OPEN_FIRE
intents.OPEN_FIRE: the bot starts shooting, or is told it is free to shoot (open fire, start shooting, weapons free, fire at will, light them up); its planner picks the targets. A place or direction in the line is where to shoot
intents.HOLD_FIRE: the bot stops shooting or must not start (hold fire, cease fire, don't shoot, stop shooting), also until something happens ('don't shoot until they come closer'). It is an order even though it is phrased as a negation. The bot may keep moving and doing other things: pausing everything is WAIT
intents.LOOK_AT: the bot turns and looks at something: a named place or object, the thing the player points at, or a direction (look at the sofa, look at that window, look left, look up, look behind you, face the door, turn around). It is one look, not a watch: keeping an angle covered, ready to shoot, is HOLD_ANGLE ('watch the window', 'eyes on the door', 'cover the stairs'); going to a place is MOVE_TO, going somewhere to check it out is DRONE. A 'look' that is not about turning to see is not this intent: a warning or an exclamation ('look out', 'look at that shot'), a filler ('look, we need to move'), searching ('look for the defuser') are NONE
intents.LOOK_AT_ME: the bot turns and looks at the PLAYER (look at me, face me, turn to me, look over here). The bot does not come to the player -- that is FOLLOW_ME -- and does not start covering them (COVER_ME)
intents.NONE: not an order to the bot: an information callout about enemies, chatter, a question, a complaint, an order the player explicitly takes back or negates, or an order the bot has no intent for. Exception: 'don't shoot' / 'don't fire' is the order HOLD_FIRE

modifiers.timing: now | on_signal -- 'on_signal' when the player says to do it on their call / when they say go / on three; otherwise 'now'
modifiers.reference: this | other | none -- 'other' when the order is about the OTHER one of two things (the other door, the other window, the other angle); 'this' when it points at a specific thing ('this wall', 'here', 'that window'); 'none' when it names no object
modifiers.target: the place on the map the BOT must act on for the order's first action -- go to, watch, open, throw at, shoot at, hide behind... -- as {object, qualifier, zone, direction, unknown_modifier}. object: one of the map's objects or null; qualifier: one of the map's qualifiers or null (also when the player named it without saying the object, e.g. 'push main' = door / main, 'take blue' = stairs / blue; a bare compass word with no object is qualifier only); zone: the floor the place is on, or the floor itself when the order is about the floor, else null. direction: up | down | left | right | forward | back when the line gives the bot's action a direction, with or without an object ('go left' = direction left only; 'go down the stairs' = stairs + down; 'the door on the left' = door + left; 'check behind you' = back), else null. A direction that describes the object is that object's: 'the door behind you' = door + back, 'the window above you' = window + up. If the line gives both the side that tells WHICH object it is and a direction of movement, give the side: 'go up the stairs on the left' = stairs + left. A word that only belongs to a fixed phrase is NOT a direction: 'fall back' and 'back up' (retreat), 'hold up', 'move up' and 'push up' (advance), 'get down' (take cover), 'two left' (remaining), 'right now', 'go ahead' (permission). 'upstairs' / 'downstairs' stay the zones up / down, with no direction. The target is NOT the player's own position, NOT where the enemy is and NOT the place to leave: 'I'll take the north door, you take the south window' -> window / south; 'I'll go left, you go right' -> direction right. unknown_modifier: true when the player singles out one particular object with a word that is neither a map name nor a direction ('the back door', 'the side door', 'the blue door', 'the second window', 'the stairs at the back': 'back', 'rear' and 'side' said of an object name a part of the building, not a direction); then give the object and leave the qualifier null. 'the left window' is NOT unknown_modifier any more: window + direction left. For a callout or chatter (intent NONE) give the place or direction the line is about, if it names one ('two on the left' = direction left). All are null / false when the line names no place of the map and no direction (a marker, 'here', 'there', 'that wall'). For LOOK_AT the target is what the bot must look at ('look at the sofa' = sofa, 'look at that window' = window, 'look left' = direction left); for LOOK_AT_ME it is the player, who is not a place of the map: all null.

map.note: Every map of the game has these named places, and players use the names in orders and callouts. Doors and windows are named by compass side, plus one Main door; stairs are named by colour; furniture and floors by what they are.

objects.door: a door: the Main door, or the north / south / west / east door
objects.window: a window: the north / south / west / east window
objects.stairs: a staircase: the blue / red / yellow / white / brown stairs

zones.floor_2: a second floor, if the player names one

directions.up: upwards: 'go up', 'up the stairs', 'look up', 'from above'
directions.down: downwards: 'go down', 'down the stairs', 'drop down', 'from below'
directions.left: to the bot's or player's left: 'go left', 'on your left', 'the left window', 'the door on the left', 'nine o'clock'
directions.right: to the right: 'go right', 'to the right', 'the right door', 'three o'clock'
directions.forward: ahead: 'move forward', 'push forward', 'straight ahead', 'in front of you', 'twelve o'clock'
directions.back: behind, backwards: 'go back', 'behind you', 'check your six', 'to the rear'
